text: The plural comprehension schema is ∃x φ(x) → ∃xx ∀x(x ≺ xx ↔ φ(x)). What is the role of the antecedent ∃x φ(x)?
choices: It ensures φ is a first-order formula
It restricts φ to set-sized collections
It guarantees the resulting plurality is nonempty, since by convention pluralities have at least one member
It blocks the formula φ from mentioning the predicate ≺
explanation: By convention every plurality has at least one member, so comprehension forms the xx only when some object actually satisfies φ; the antecedent ∃x φ(x) enforces this nonemptiness. It says nothing about φ's order or 'set-size,' and it is the separate proviso 'xx not free in φ' — not the antecedent — that blocks the self-referential ¬(x ≺ xx).
